facts.value: Psychological testing has ancient origins, dating back to 2200 BCE in the examinations for the Chinese civil service.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: Written exams began during the Han dynasty (202 BCE – 220 CE).
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: By 1370, the Chinese system required a stratified series of tests, involving essay writing and knowledge of diverse topics.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: In Europe, mental assessment took a different approach, with theories of physiognomy described by Aristotle in 4th century BCE Greece.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: Francis Galton is considered an inventor of modern mental testing.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: James McKeen Cattell coined the term 'mental test'.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: Alfred Binet and Théodore Simon developed a new test of intelligence in 1905–1911 and introduced the concept of 'mental age'.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: In 1916, Lewis M. Terman modified the Binet-Simon scale, renaming it the Stanford–Binet scale and introduced the intelligence quotient as a score report.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: Robert Yerkes developed the Army Alpha and Army Beta tests in 1917, used in World War I for large-scale employee testing and selection of military personnel.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: In the 1920s, the federally created National Intelligence Test was administered to 7 million children in the U.S.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: Today, mental testing is a routine phenomenon for people of all ages in Western societies.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: Modern testing aspires to criteria including standardization of procedure, consistency of results, output of an interpretable score, statistical norms, and effective prediction of behavior and life outcomes.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick
